headline: Open-source workflows for curating morphology, biodiversity, and fungal RNA-seq data
label: Open Shared Biological Data Infrastructure
summary: Open development practices and AI-ready outputs are being applied to shared 3D, biodiversity, and transcriptomic datasets.
synthesis: The common thread is packaging shared biological data and analysis as open, reusable infrastructure with explicit provenance. MorphoDepot transfers git and GitHub fork-and-contribute workflows into 3D digital morphology, using 3D Slicer and SlicerMorph to community-curate segmented anatomical datasets. cheCkOVER provides a GPL-3 framework that converts crayfish occurrence records into provenance-tracked JSON and maps designed for API access and AI retrieval. BRC-Analytics pairs an agentic AI assistant with Galaxy tools to standardize RNA-seq analysis, reanalyzing two studies of Candidozyma auris. The domains differ, and the summaries describe architectures rather than comparative performance. What is new is the emphasis on version-controlled contribution, machine-readable provenance, and reproducible execution as the unit of data sharing. The evidence is descriptive; none of the summaries report benchmarks against alternative tools.
